html:
SMTO-EXE-0158 — The computer's security settings blocked this desktop action

GUID: 696aa043-f067-5080-a4aa-bb400b7bce12
Slug: ui-platform-permission-required
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • The operating system on the Gateway's computer refused SMTO's click, key press or change in the app. SMTO can't be sure whether part of the action went through before it was refused.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On a Mac, open System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility on the Gateway's computer and turn on the app that runs the Gateway. macOS blocks automated clicks and typing until that permission is turned on.
  2. Make sure the app is in a normal signed-in desktop, not behind a lock screen or a Windows administrator prompt (User Account Control). Operating systems block automated input to lock screens and administrator prompts on purpose.
  3. If the app was started with Run as administrator, restart it normally, or do that step yourself. Windows blocks a normal program from sending input to an app running as administrator.
  4. Before asking SMTO to try again, look at the app to see whether part of the action already happened. Some keys or clicks may have gone through before the computer refused the rest.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next desktop step in that app works without this message, and the app shows the change only once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway's computer. Don't turn off protections such as User Account Control to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A native Desktop UI API (macOS AX set-attribute, AT-SPI action, Windows SendInput or SetCursorPos, or a key release) refused the request; the exact OS cause, often missing accessibility permission or privilege isolation, is not established.

What this means

  • A native semantic/input API refused the request or reported a permission-related failure, including failed key release or pointer movement. Exact OS cause is not always established. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • A native semantic/input API refused the request or reported a permission-related failure, including failed key release or pointer movement. Exact OS cause is not always established.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect session, native permission and original action state without bypassing secure desktop or privilege isolation.

How to fix it

  • Run the Gateway in the target user's interactive session and grant native accessibility/input permission (macOS: System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility for the Gateway host; Windows: same integrity level as the target app, not UAC or Secure Desktop; Linux: an app that supports the AT-SPI action). Inspect ui.snapshot to reconcile any partial effect before repeating.
  • Use the target interactive user session and grant native accessibility permission. Do not bypass UAC, Secure Desktop or application privilege isolation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the target interactive user session and grant native accessibility permission. Do not bypass UAC, Secure Desktop or application privilege isolation.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended action is supported under authorized permissions and any prior attempted effect is reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
